_what_this_is: An ADVERSARIAL application of NCP v0.1 to Consullo's EXISTING checks. Every negative control was EXECUTED against a deliberately broken build; nothing here was inferred from reading source. It is NON-CONFORMING, which is the result, not a defect in the attestation.
_abstracted: ABSTRACTED 2026-08-10 at the implementer's direction. Files, classes and configuration keys are described by ROLE. The IMPLEMENTER is still named: Consullo published its own submission under its own name, so concealing whose system this is would be incoherent as well as pointless. What is removed is how the code works. What was removed is identifying detail about a private codebase; what is kept is every outcome, every perturbation, and every artifact hash -- the parts that carry evidentiary weight. The prior version named them and remains in this repository's git history, which abstraction cannot reach and this note does not pretend otherwise. See record/designs/implementer-disclosure.md.

checks.role: first stage of a deployment health script; tests that the service port accepts a TCP connection

negative_control.condition: the capability behind the port is dead while the process still holds the socket
negative_control.how_produced: a process bound to the service port that accepts connections and serves nothing (spec/ncp/negative-controls/broken_socket_only.py)
negative_control.targets: the declared capability, not the transport

run.method: EXECUTED against a deliberately broken build
run.note: the probe reported the port open and exited 0. THE CHECK SURVIVES ITS OWN NEGATIVE CONTROL. A TCP-accept test cannot distinguish a working service from a dead one behind a live socket, which is the recorded production failure state.

checks.role: second stage of the same script; tests that the health endpoint answers

negative_control.condition: the endpoint answers, and answers that it is UNHEALTHY
negative_control.how_produced: a server returning HTTP 503 with a body whose status field is 'unhealthy' (spec/ncp/negative-controls/broken_unhealthy.py)
negative_control.targets: the declared capability, not the transport

run.method: EXECUTED against a deliberately broken build
run.note: the probe reported the application responsive and exited 0. It matches on the presence of the status FIELD and never reads its VALUE, and it fetches without failing on HTTP error status, so a 503 body satisfies it. A later stage does catch this; ORDERING is the only thing between this check and a false green.

checks.role: aggregates per-component health into one overall verdict

negative_control.condition: the database check is DISABLED by configuration
negative_control.how_produced: the aggregator driven directly with the database-check flag set false
negative_control.targets: the declared capability, not the transport

run.note: the overall verdict remained healthy and the database component was ABSENT from the output entirely -- not reported as skipped, simply not there. A consumer cannot distinguish 'healthy' from 'never checked'. This violates the implementer's own submitted pattern requiring disclosure of skipped, suppressed and unsupported checks.

checks.role: the same aggregator under a development-mode concession

negative_control.condition: the database is UNAVAILABLE while development mode is on
negative_control.how_produced: the aggregator driven directly with no database present, development-mode flag true, then again with it false
negative_control.targets: the declared capability, not the transport

run.note: with the flag on, the overall verdict was healthy while the database component read unavailable. With the flag off, the same conditions gave an unhealthy verdict. The concession is disclosed in a nested component message, but the TOP-LEVEL verdict is what consumers read -- it selects the HTTP response code and is what the responsiveness probe greps. A consumer reading the verdict never reaches the message.

negative_control.correction: An earlier version of the finding said the response does not record that development mode is in force. THAT WAS WRONG: a nested component message names it. The claim was asserted from reading the verdict logic without reading the message string -- a smaller instance of the reading error the whole assessment is about, and execution is what caught it.

checks.role: a watchdog probe that actively tests whether the serving engine can still complete a request on the sampled decode path
checks.certifies: the engine can complete a sampled (temperature > 0) request

negative_control.condition: the sampled decode path is dead while the process still serves HTTP
negative_control.how_produced: the recorded production failure: a lazily-compiled kernel on the sampled path failed on first use and killed the executor permanently
negative_control.targets: the declared capability, not the transport

run.note: the canary requests at a non-zero temperature, which reaches the sampling code that died; a greedy request would execute none of it. This is the ONE check assessed with a demonstrated failure mode, and it has one because it was rebuilt AFTER the outage its predecessor could not see.

unsupported: N5 relevance -- that a control perturbs the capability rather than the transport -- is a declared field a human must judge; nothing checks it.

claim: Five checks of the Consullo enterprise layer were assessed against NCP v0.1, with every negative control EXECUTED against a deliberately broken build. FOUR survive their own negative controls and are therefore not evidence that anything works. One fails under its control and conforms. This is process evidence about the checks and is not a claim about the system.
